citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.
Let $0<r<R$ and $n\ge 1$. Then there exists a smooth function $\rho:\mathbb R^n\to [0,1]$ such that $\rho=1$ on $\overline B_r(0)$ and $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)\subseteq B_R(0)$.

In ZF, for compact $K\subseteq\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ with $\Omega$ open, there is $\chi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ with $0\le\chi\le1$ and $\chi=1$ on a neighborhood of $K$. Every open cover of $\Omega$ admits an at most countable locally finite smooth partition of unity with compact supports, each support contained in some cover member. Subordination here asserts existence of such a member for each support; it does not select cover labels.

For the Lebesgue branches (a) and (b) assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), inherited from the exact measure interface ([[def-countable-choice]]); the finite sums in branch (c) are defined and computed without Choice. Let the laboratory region, its chart, its spatial Euclidean structure and its units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $\delta_{ij}$ be the Kronecker symbol in the $\delta$-orthonormal basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of the frame, with $|y|$ the Euclidean norm of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. This definition assigns **source moments** to a static charge distribution in the fixed-time reading of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (d) and (e). Three branches are declared.

(a) [Absolutely continuous branch] Let $a>0$ and let $\rho\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ be real ([[def-l-one-of-a-measure]]) and vanish $\lambda_3$-almost everywhere outside the closed ball $\overline B_a(0)=\{y:|y|\le a\}$ ([[def-metric-ball]], [[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]]). The **total charge** $Q$, the **dipole moment** $p$, the **degree-$l$ Cartesian moments** $M_{i_1\dots i_l}$ and the **traceless quadrupole** $Q_{ij}$ are

$$Q:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\rho\,d\lambda_3,\qquad p_i:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}y_i\,\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y),\qquad M_{i_1\dots i_l}:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}y_{i_1}\cdots y_{i_l}\,\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y)\ (l\ge1),$$

$$M^{(0)}:=Q,\qquad M_i:=p_i,\qquad Q_{ij}:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\bigl(3y_iy_j-|y|^2\delta_{ij}\bigr)\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y),$$

with $l\ge1$ and indices in $\{1,2,3\}$; units are C for $Q$, C m for $p$, C m$^l$ for the degree-$l$ Cartesian moment and C m$^2$ for $Q_{ij}$, and all integrals are in the sense of [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]] and [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]. Each integral is absolutely convergent: since $\rho=0$ $\lambda_3$-a.e. off $\overline B_a(0)$, and the maps $y\mapsto y_{i_1}\cdots y_{i_l}$ and $y\mapsto 3y_iy_j-|y|^2\delta_{ij}$ are bounded $\lambda_3$-a.e. on that ball by $a^l$ and by $4a^2$ respectively, the integrands are dominated $\lambda_3$-a.e. by $a^l|\rho|$ and $4a^2|\rho|$, which lie in $L^1$ ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]). The traceless quadrupole is traceless,

$$\sum_{i=1}^3Q_{ii}=0,$$

because $\sum_{i=1}^3(3y_i^2-|y|^2)=0$ pointwise, and summing the three integrable functions $3y_i^2\rho-|y|^2\rho$ and applying finite linearity of the integral on $L^1$ ([[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]) evaluates the sum as the integral of the pointwise-zero function; replacing $\rho$ by an equal $\lambda_3$-a.e. density changes no moment ([[thm-the-lebesgue-integral-respects-almost-everywhere-equality]]).

(b) [General locally integrable branch] If instead $\rho\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^3)$ is real and $\int_{\mathbb R^3}|y|^l|\rho(y)|\,d\lambda_3(y)<\infty$ for a given integer $l\ge0$, then the degree-$l$ Cartesian moments of the same formula are absolutely convergent and defined; if the absolute weighted moment $\int_{\mathbb R^3}|y|^L|\rho(y)|\,d\lambda_3(y)$ is finite for some real $L\ge0$, then every integer Cartesian degree $0\le l\le L$ is defined, and in particular $Q=\int\rho\,d\lambda_3$ is absolutely convergent, so that $\rho\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ is a conclusion of this branch and not an added hypothesis. If $f$ is $C^2$ on an open subset of $\mathbb R^m$, then $\partial_i\partial_j f=\partial_j\partial_i f$ for every pair of coordinate indices.

$$0<\lambda(B(x,r))<\infty.$$

1. If $f\le g$, then $\int f\,d\mu\le\int g\,d\mu$.
2. If $c>0$, then $\int cf\,d\mu=c\int f\,d\mu$. For $c=0$,
   the integral of the zero function is $0$. Neither clause forms the

$$\lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S^2}r^2n\cdot S(rn,u+r/c)\,d\Omega(n)=\frac{\mu_0}{16\pi^2c}\int_{S^2}|n\times V(n,u)|^2\,d\Omega(n).$$

Define $G(t):=\chi_G(t)(t-u)^2$ and $H(t):=\chi_H(t)(t-u)^3$. Then $G''(u)=2$ and $H'''(s)=6$ for every $s\in[u-a/c,u+a/c]$.

Let $e_1=(1,0,0)$ and $e_3=(0,0,1)$, and define $\displaystyle \rho(y,t):=-G(t)\partial_3f(y),\qquad J(y,t):=G'(t)f(y)e_3+H'(t)\bigl(-\partial_3f(y)e_1+\partial_1f(y)e_3\bigr).$ These maps are jointly smooth and supported in $\operatorname{supp}f\times(\operatorname{supp}G\cup\operatorname{supp}G'\cup\operatorname{supp}H')$, a compact subset of $B_a\times\mathbb R$. Their derivatives satisfy $\displaystyle \partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}_yJ=-G'(t)\partial_3f+G'(t)\partial_3f+H'(t)(-\partial_1\partial_3f+\partial_3\partial_1f)=0$ by [F4], so the source is admissible for the controlled multipole theorem.

The current derivative is $J_t=G''f e_3+H''(-\partial_3f\,e_1+\partial_1f\,e_3)$. Each integral $\int_{\mathbb R^3}\partial_i f\,dy$ is zero by the divergence theorem applied to $f e_i$ on a ball containing $\operatorname{supp}f$, since its boundary flux vanishes. Thus [F3] gives $p''(u)=\int J_t(y,u)\,dy=G''(u)F e_3=2F e_3$, which is nonzero and parallel to $n=e_3$. Therefore $n\times(n\times p''(u))=0$.

For $n=e_3$, the $e_1$ component of the exact shifted current moment is $\displaystyle V_1(e_3,u)=-\int_{B_a}H''(u+y_3/c)\partial_3f(y)\,dy=\frac1c\int_{B_a}f(y)H'''(u+y_3/c)\,dy=\frac{6F}{c}>0.$ The middle equality is integration by parts in $y_3$; the boundary term vanishes because $f$ has compact support, and $|y_3|\le a$ on its support, so $H'''=6$ there by step 1.1. The term $G''f e_3$ contributes no $e_1$ component. Hence $V(e_3,u)$ has a nonzero component perpendicular to $e_3$.

By [F6], $E_{\mathrm{rad}}(e_3,u)=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}e_3\times(e_3\times V(e_3,u))\ne0$, whereas the dipole coefficient $\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}e_3\times(e_3\times p''(u))$ is zero by step 3.1. supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the source, SI and retarded-field hypotheses of the preceding transverse-radiation theorem on a nondegenerate compact retarded-time interval $K$. Fix an integer $N\ge0$. Define the $N$th finite retarded-current Taylor coefficient by

$$\mathcal J_N(n,u):=\sum_{k=0}^{N}\frac{1}{k!\,c^k}\int_{B_a}(n\cdot y)^k\,\partial_t^{k+1}J(y,u)\,dy,$$

and define the source-scale remainder

$$\mathcal R_N(u):=\frac{a^{N+1}}{(N+1)!\,c^{N+1}}\int_{B_a}\sup_{|s-u|\le a/c}\left|\partial_t^{N+2}J(y,s)\right|\,dy.$$

The coefficient $\mathcal J_N$ and the remainder $\mathcal R_N$ both have units $\mathrm A\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$. The supremum is finite and integrable in $y$. Let

$$A_N(u):=\sup_{n\in S^2}|\mathcal J_N(n,u)|,\qquad P(u):=\lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S^2}r^2n\cdot S(rn,u+r/c)\,d\Omega(n),$$

where $P(u)$ exists by the preceding theorem. Then uniformly for $n\in S^2$ and $u\in K$,

$$|V(n,u)-\mathcal J_N(n,u)|\le\mathcal R_N(u),$$

$$\left|E(rn,u+r/c)-\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi r}n\times(n\times\mathcal J_N(n,u))\right|\le\frac{\Gamma_E}{r^2}+\frac{\mu_0\mathcal R_N(u)}{4\pi r}\qquad(r\ge2a),$$

$$\left|P(u)-\frac{\mu_0}{16\pi^2c}\int_{S^2}|n\times\mathcal J_N(n,u)|^2\,d\Omega(n)\right|\le\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi c}\bigl(2A_N(u)+\mathcal R_N(u)\bigr)\mathcal R_N(u).$$

For $N=0$, $\mathcal J_0(n,u)=p''(u)$ for the time-dependent electric dipole moment $p(u):=\int_{B_a}y\rho(y,u)\,dy$, and $\mathcal R_0(u)=\frac ac\int_{B_a}\sup_{|s-u|\le a/c}|J_{tt}(y,s)|\,dy$. Consequently

$$\left|P(u)-\frac{\mu_0}{6\pi c}|p''(u)|^2\right|\le\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi c}\left(2|p''(u)|\mathcal R_0(u)+\mathcal R_0(u)^2\right).$$

Every finite truncation has its own explicit derivative remainder. No convergence of the infinite Taylor series and no relative error at an angular node are asserted.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Use the SI laboratory chart and source conventions: $\rho:\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ has units $\mathrm C\,\mathrm m^{-3}$ and $J:\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ has units $\mathrm A\,\mathrm m^{-2}$. Let $a,c,\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$, and let $\rho,J$ be jointly $C^\infty$, vanish for $|y|>a$, and satisfy $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}_yJ=0$. Let $K=[u_-,u_+]\subset\mathbb R$ be a nondegenerate compact interval, $u_-<u_+$, and put $K^\sharp=[u_--2a/c,u_++2a/c]$. For $j=0,1,2$, define

$$M_{\rho,j}:=\sup_{\overline B_a\times K^\sharp}|\partial_t^j\rho|,\qquad M_{J,j}:=\sup_{\overline B_a\times K^\sharp}|\partial_t^jJ|.$$

For $n\in S^2$ and $u\in K$, define the retarded current moment and its derivative by

$$I(n,u):=\int_{B_a}J(y,u+n\cdot y/c)\,dy,\qquad V(n,u):=\partial_u I(n,u)=\int_{B_a}J_t(y,u+n\cdot y/c)\,dy.$$

Let $E,B$ be the selected retarded fields of the preceding theorem, set $S=E\times B/\mu_0$, and define

$$\Gamma_E:=\frac{\mu_0\lambda_3(B_a)}{4\pi}\left(4c^2M_{\rho,0}+13caM_{\rho,1}+a^2M_{\rho,2}+3aM_{J,1}+\frac{a^2}{c}M_{J,2}\right),$$

$$\Gamma_B:=\frac{\mu_0\lambda_3(B_a)}{4\pi}\left(4M_{J,0}+\frac{13a}{c}M_{J,1}+\frac{a^2}{c^2}M_{J,2}\right).$$

Then for every $n\in S^2$, $u\in K$ and $r\ge2a$, with $E_{\mathrm{lead}}(n,u,r):=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi r}n\times(n\times V(n,u))$,

$$\left|E(rn,u+r/c)-E_{\mathrm{lead}}(n,u,r)\right|\le\frac{\Gamma_E}{r^2},\qquad \left|B(rn,u+r/c)-\frac{n\times E_{\mathrm{lead}}(n,u,r)}{c}\right|\le\frac{\Gamma_B}{r^2}.$$

Consequently the radiation data of the preceding definition exist uniformly on $S^2\times K$ and equal

$$E_{\mathrm{rad}}(n,u)=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}n\times(n\times V(n,u)),\qquad B_{\mathrm{rad}}(n,u)=\frac{n\times E_{\mathrm{rad}}(n,u)}{c}.$$

For each fixed retarded time $u$, the outward retarded-time flux has the exact limit

$$\lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S^2}r^2n\cdot S(rn,u+r/c)\,d\Omega(n)=\frac{\mu_0}{16\pi^2c}\int_{S^2}|n\times V(n,u)|^2\,d\Omega(n).$$

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.
Let $0<r<R$ and $n\ge 1$. Then there exists a smooth function $\rho:\mathbb R^n\to [0,1]$ such that $\rho=1$ on $\overline B_r(0)$ and $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)\subseteq B_R(0)$.

In ZF, for compact $K\subseteq\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ with $\Omega$ open, there is $\chi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ with $0\le\chi\le1$ and $\chi=1$ on a neighborhood of $K$. Every open cover of $\Omega$ admits an at most countable locally finite smooth partition of unity with compact supports, each support contained in some cover member. Subordination here asserts existence of such a member for each support; it does not select cover labels.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $a,c,\mu_0>0$, let $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$, and let $\rho:\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ and $J:\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ be jointly $C^\infty$. Suppose $\rho(y,t)=J(y,t)=0$ whenever $|y|>a$ and suppose the continuity equation $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}_yJ=0$ holds everywhere.

Adopt the smooth vacuum Maxwell equations and the retarded, no-free-addition selection as the physical model assumptions. In the SI laboratory convention, define

$$\varphi(x,t):=\frac{\mu_0c^2}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{\rho(y,t-|x-y|/c)}{|x-y|}\,dy,\qquad A(x,t):=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{J(y,t-|x-y|/c)}{|x-y|}\,dy.$$

The integrals converge absolutely at every $(x,t)$. The resulting potentials are jointly $C^\infty$ and satisfy $W\varphi=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $WA=\mu_0J$, and $\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi=0$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, where $W=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta$. Consequently $E=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$ and $B=\operatorname{curl}A$ are jointly smooth and satisfy the smooth vacuum Maxwell equations for $(\rho,J)$ everywhere. This is the selected retarded solution, with no independent homogeneous field added. No compact support in time is assumed.

Assume Countable Choice. Use the SI laboratory chart and source conventions: $\rho:\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ has units $\mathrm C\,\mathrm m^{-3}$ and $J:\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ has units $\mathrm A\,\mathrm m^{-2}$. Let $a,c,\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$, and let $\rho,J$ be jointly $C^\infty$, vanish for $|y|>a$, and satisfy $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}_yJ=0$. Let $K=[u_-,u_+]\subset\mathbb R$ be a nondegenerate compact interval, $u_-<u_+$, and put $K^\sharp=[u_--2a/c,u_++2a/c]$. For $j=0,1,2$, define

$$M_{\rho,j}:=\sup_{\overline B_a\times K^\sharp}|\partial_t^j\rho|,\qquad M_{J,j}:=\sup_{\overline B_a\times K^\sharp}|\partial_t^jJ|.$$

For $n\in S^2$ and $u\in K$, define the retarded current moment and its derivative by

$$I(n,u):=\int_{B_a}J(y,u+n\cdot y/c)\,dy,\qquad V(n,u):=\partial_u I(n,u)=\int_{B_a}J_t(y,u+n\cdot y/c)\,dy.$$

Let $E,B$ be the selected retarded fields of the preceding theorem, set $S=E\times B/\mu_0$, and define

$$\Gamma_E:=\frac{\mu_0\lambda_3(B_a)}{4\pi}\left(4c^2M_{\rho,0}+13caM_{\rho,1}+a^2M_{\rho,2}+3aM_{J,1}+\frac{a^2}{c}M_{J,2}\right),$$

$$\Gamma_B:=\frac{\mu_0\lambda_3(B_a)}{4\pi}\left(4M_{J,0}+\frac{13a}{c}M_{J,1}+\frac{a^2}{c^2}M_{J,2}\right).$$

Then for every $n\in S^2$, $u\in K$ and $r\ge2a$, with $E_{\mathrm{lead}}(n,u,r):=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi r}n\times(n\times V(n,u))$,

$$\left|E(rn,u+r/c)-E_{\mathrm{lead}}(n,u,r)\right|\le\frac{\Gamma_E}{r^2},\qquad \left|B(rn,u+r/c)-\frac{n\times E_{\mathrm{lead}}(n,u,r)}{c}\right|\le\frac{\Gamma_B}{r^2}.$$

Consequently the radiation data of the preceding definition exist uniformly on $S^2\times K$ and equal

$$E_{\mathrm{rad}}(n,u)=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}n\times(n\times V(n,u)),\qquad B_{\mathrm{rad}}(n,u)=\frac{n\times E_{\mathrm{rad}}(n,u)}{c}.$$

For each fixed retarded time $u$, the outward retarded-time flux has the exact limit

$$\lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S^2}r^2n\cdot S(rn,u+r/c)\,d\Omega(n)=\frac{\mu_0}{16\pi^2c}\int_{S^2}|n\times V(n,u)|^2\,d\Omega(n).$$

Let the laboratory frame and SI conventions be those of the framework, and let $\rho,J$ be a jointly smooth conserved volume source supported in $\overline B_a(0)$ in space at every time, for some $a>0$. Let $E,B$ be the retarded fields generated by that source. Write $S^2=\{n\in\mathbb R^3:|n|=1\}$, $r=|x|$, and $t=u+r/c$. If maps $E_{\mathrm{rad}},B_{\mathrm{rad}}:S^2\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ satisfy

$$rE(rn,u+r/c)\longrightarrow E_{\mathrm{rad}}(n,u),\qquad rB(rn,u+r/c)\longrightarrow B_{\mathrm{rad}}(n,u)$$

uniformly in $n\in S^2$ and $u$ in every compact interval as $r\to\infty$, then $E_{\mathrm{rad}}$ and $B_{\mathrm{rad}}$ are the electric and magnetic radiation data at fixed retarded time. The scaled fields carry units $\mathrm V$ and $\mathrm T\,\mathrm m$, respectively. This definition by itself does not assert that the limits exist.
If $f$ is $C^2$ on an open subset of $\mathbb R^m$, then $\partial_i\partial_j f=\partial_j\partial_i f$ for every pair of coordinate indices.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be an arbitrary measure space. Let $f,g:X\to[0,+\infty]$ be measurable and let $c\ge0$.

1. If $f\le g$, then $\int f\,d\mu\le\int g\,d\mu$.
2. If $c>0$, then $\int cf\,d\mu=c\int f\,d\mu$. For $c=0$,
   the integral of the zero function is $0$. Neither clause forms the
   undefined extended-real product $0\cdot(+\infty)$.

derivations.claim: By [F1] choose $f\in C_c^\infty(B_a(0))$ with $0\le f\le1$ and $f=1$ on some ball $B_{r_0}(0)$ with $0<r_0<a$. Then $F:=\int f\,dy\ge\lambda_3(B_{r_0})>0$ by [F3]. Choose $G$ by applying the smooth cutoff supplier to a compact interval slightly larger than $[u-a/c,u+a/c]$ and multiply that cutoff by $(t-u)^2$. The resulting $G$ is compactly supported, equals $(t-u)^2$ on a neighborhood of the delay interval, and satisfies $G''(u)=2$.

The maps $\rho,J$ in the Example are jointly smooth and compactly supported in $B_a$ in space and in $\operatorname{supp}G\cup\operatorname{supp}G'$ in time. Their derivatives obey $\rho_t=-G'\partial_3f$ and $\operatorname{div}J=G'\partial_3f$, so $\rho_t+\operatorname{div}J=0$. Thus the retarded-history theorem applies.

For $n=e_1$, every source point in $B_a$ has $|y_1|<a$, so $G''(u+y_1/c)=2$. The shifted-current moment of [F2] is therefore $\displaystyle V(e_1,u)=\int_{B_a}J_t(y,u+y_1/c)\,dy=G''(u)\left(\int_{B_a}f(y)\,dy\right)e_3=2F e_3.$ Since $e_1\cdot e_3=0$, $e_1\times(e_1\times V(e_1,u))=-2F e_3\ne0$. The radiation-data formula [F2] now gives $\displaystyle E_{\mathrm{rad}}(e_1,u)=-\frac{\mu_0F}{2\pi}e_3\ne0,$ so $rE(re_1,u+r/c)$ converges to a nonzero vector.

Let $t_f\in\mathbb R$ be a fixed observation time and choose $t_-<\inf(\operatorname{supp}G\cup\operatorname{supp}G')$. For $y\in B_a$ and $x=rn$, $|x-y|\ge r-a$, so the source retarded time satisfies $t_f-|x-y|/c\le t_f-(r-a)/c$. If $r>a+c(t_f-t_-)$, this is less than $t_-$ for every $y\in B_a$, with a uniform strict margin. The source and all its derivatives vanish on a time neighborhood of every such argument; because the inequalities remain strict on a neighborhood of $(x,t_f)$, the retarded potentials are identically zero there and their derivatives vanish. Hence $E(rn,t_f)=B(rn,t_f)=0$ for all such $r$. This fixed-time limit and the nonzero scaled retarded-time limit of step 3.1 are different paths to infinity, not contradictory field values.

Example and steps 1.1 and 3.1: a,c>0, the bump integral F>0 and G is quadratic throughout the closed delay window. Thus the selected radiation moment is 2F e3, nonzero; no nondegenerate K assumption is imposed.

Let $n\ge1$, let $x\in\mathbb{R}^n$, and let $r>0$. Then the Euclidean ball $B(x,r)$ is
Lebesgue measurable and satisfies
$$0<\lambda(B(x,r))<\infty.$$

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $a,c,\mu_0>0$, let $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$, and let $\rho:\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ and $J:\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ be jointly $C^\infty$. Suppose $\rho(y,t)=J(y,t)=0$ whenever $|y|>a$ and suppose the continuity equation $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}_yJ=0$ holds everywhere.

Adopt the smooth vacuum Maxwell equations and the retarded, no-free-addition selection as the physical model assumptions. In the SI laboratory convention, define

$$\varphi(x,t):=\frac{\mu_0c^2}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{\rho(y,t-|x-y|/c)}{|x-y|}\,dy,\qquad A(x,t):=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{J(y,t-|x-y|/c)}{|x-y|}\,dy.$$

The integrals converge absolutely at every $(x,t)$. The resulting potentials are jointly $C^\infty$ and satisfy $W\varphi=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $WA=\mu_0J$, and $\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi=0$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, where $W=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta$. Consequently $E=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$ and $B=\operatorname{curl}A$ are jointly smooth and satisfy the smooth vacuum Maxwell equations for $(\rho,J)$ everywhere. This is the selected retarded solution, with no independent homogeneous field added. No compact support in time is assumed.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Use the SI laboratory chart and source conventions: $\rho:\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ has units $\mathrm C\,\mathrm m^{-3}$ and $J:\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ has units $\mathrm A\,\mathrm m^{-2}$. Let $a,c,\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$, and let $\rho,J$ be jointly $C^\infty$, vanish for $|y|>a$, and satisfy $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}_yJ=0$. Let $K=[u_-,u_+]\subset\mathbb R$ be a nondegenerate compact interval, $u_-<u_+$, and put $K^\sharp=[u_--2a/c,u_++2a/c]$. For $j=0,1,2$, define

$$M_{\rho,j}:=\sup_{\overline B_a\times K^\sharp}|\partial_t^j\rho|,\qquad M_{J,j}:=\sup_{\overline B_a\times K^\sharp}|\partial_t^jJ|.$$

For $n\in S^2$ and $u\in K$, define the retarded current moment and its derivative by

$$I(n,u):=\int_{B_a}J(y,u+n\cdot y/c)\,dy,\qquad V(n,u):=\partial_u I(n,u)=\int_{B_a}J_t(y,u+n\cdot y/c)\,dy.$$

Let $E,B$ be the selected retarded fields of the preceding theorem, set $S=E\times B/\mu_0$, and define

$$\Gamma_E:=\frac{\mu_0\lambda_3(B_a)}{4\pi}\left(4c^2M_{\rho,0}+13caM_{\rho,1}+a^2M_{\rho,2}+3aM_{J,1}+\frac{a^2}{c}M_{J,2}\right),$$

$$\Gamma_B:=\frac{\mu_0\lambda_3(B_a)}{4\pi}\left(4M_{J,0}+\frac{13a}{c}M_{J,1}+\frac{a^2}{c^2}M_{J,2}\right).$$

Then for every $n\in S^2$, $u\in K$ and $r\ge2a$, with $E_{\mathrm{lead}}(n,u,r):=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi r}n\times(n\times V(n,u))$,

$$\left|E(rn,u+r/c)-E_{\mathrm{lead}}(n,u,r)\right|\le\frac{\Gamma_E}{r^2},\qquad \left|B(rn,u+r/c)-\frac{n\times E_{\mathrm{lead}}(n,u,r)}{c}\right|\le\frac{\Gamma_B}{r^2}.$$

Consequently the radiation data of the preceding definition exist uniformly on $S^2\times K$ and equal

$$E_{\mathrm{rad}}(n,u)=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}n\times(n\times V(n,u)),\qquad B_{\mathrm{rad}}(n,u)=\frac{n\times E_{\mathrm{rad}}(n,u)}{c}.$$

For each fixed retarded time $u$, the outward retarded-time flux has the exact limit

$$\lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S^2}r^2n\cdot S(rn,u+r/c)\,d\Omega(n)=\frac{\mu_0}{16\pi^2c}\int_{S^2}|n\times V(n,u)|^2\,d\Omega(n).$$

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be an arbitrary measure space. Let $f,g:X\to[0,+\infty]$ be measurable and let $c\ge0$.

1. If $f\le g$, then $\int f\,d\mu\le\int g\,d\mu$.
2. If $c>0$, then $\int cf\,d\mu=c\int f\,d\mu$. For $c=0$,
   the integral of the zero function is $0$. Neither clause forms the
   undefined extended-real product $0\cdot(+\infty)$.
